stories.headline: Alphabet Sells Record ¥576.5B ($3.6B) in Debut Yen Bond, the Biggest Ever by a Non-Japanese Issuer

key_facts.fact: Alphabet sold ¥576.5 billion ($3.6 billion) of yen-denominated bonds on May 15, the largest-ever yen deal by a non-Japanese company, breaking Berkshire Hathaway's 2019 record.
The debut yen offering came in multiple tranches with maturities from 3 to 40 years and coupons between 1.965% and 4.599%; the five-year tranche of ¥200.5 billion priced at 50 bps over mid-swaps.

Alphabet plans capital expenditures of up to $190 billion in 2026 to expand AI infrastructure and is broadening funding channels beyond US dollars after recent issuances in euros, sterling, Canadian dollars and Swiss francs.

stories.headline: Anthropic Publishes 2028 Policy Paper Urging US to Tighten Chip Controls and Curb Distillation to Hold AI Lead

key_facts.fact: In a new paper released May 14, Anthropic argues democracies can secure a commanding AI lead by 2028 if the US tightens controls on advanced compute to PRC labs, disrupts distillation of US models, and accelerates AI adoption among allies.
Anthropic warns that without action the US faces a 'destabilizing neck-and-neck race with the CCP two years from now'.

The paper says PRC labs benefit from access to export-controlled US chips via smuggling and foreign data centers, and that closing those loopholes would lower China's compute ceiling and impair distillation attacks.
Anthropic also calls on the Trump administration to 'champion the export of American AI', promoting global adoption of US-developed hardware and models to deny China footholds.

stories.headline: Anthropic Agrees Terms of $30B Round at $900B Valuation; Sequoia, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Altimeter Co-Lead

key_facts.fact: Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia Capital and Altimeter Capital have agreed to co-lead a $30 billion round into Anthropic at a $900 billion pre-money valuation.
The new valuation nearly triples Anthropic's last valuation of $350-380 billion fetched in a fundraising in early February.
Anthropic reached $30 billion in annualized revenue earlier this month, up from roughly $10 billion in 2025.
A round at this valuation would push Anthropic past OpenAI, last valued at just over $850 billion in late March.

stories.headline: Anthropic and Gates Foundation Pledge $200M Over Four Years to Deploy Claude in Global Health and Education

key_facts.fact: Anthropic and the Gates Foundation announced a $200 million, four-year partnership on May 14 covering global health, life sciences, education and economic mobility.
Anthropic's half is technical staff support and Claude usage credits; the Gates Foundation provides grant funding, program design and expertise.
The partnership will work with the Institute for Disease Modeling on forecasting malaria and tuberculosis, and with research centers using Claude to predict drug candidates for HPV and preeclampsia.
The deal is roughly four times the $50 million pact the Gates Foundation announced with OpenAI in January to support 1,000 African clinics by 2028.

stories.headline: AtkinsRéalis Q1 Profit Jumps 34% as Nuclear Bet Targets AI Data Center Power Demand

key_facts.fact: AtkinsRéalis reported a 34% year-over-year jump in Q1 profits on May 14, driven by its nuclear business as the engineering company banks on the technology to seize on AI data center power demand.
On Wednesday May 13, AtkinsRéalis signed a 20-year agreement with First American Nuclear to design and oversee construction of small modular reactor projects in North America.

Preliminary work is underway at Ontario's Pickering nuclear plant after AtkinsRéalis and Aecon signed a $2.1-billion contract to extend the life of four reactors, and the company secured a 2025 deal to extend a Cernavoda reactor and earlier won a contract to build two new multibillion-dollar reactors in Romania.
In March, AtkinsRéalis announced a partnership with Nvidia to ramp up deployment of nuclear-powered AI factories, exploring how to integrate Nvidia's technologies into the facilities.

A CANDU full-size reactor built by Candu Energy, an AtkinsRéalis subsidiary, takes about seven years to plan and build, and 'nuclear remains the primary growth engine,' per National Bank analyst Maxim Sytchev.

stories.headline: Biogen Reports First Phase 2 Tau-Targeting ASO to Show Both Pathology Reduction and Cognitive Benefit in Early Alzheimer's

key_facts.fact: Biogen on May 14 announced topline Phase 2 CELIA results for diranersen (BIIB080), an antisense oligonucleotide targeting tau, in early Alzheimer's — the first randomized Phase 2 of a tau-directed therapy to show both biomarker impact and cognitive benefit.
The primary endpoint of CELIA was the assessment of dose change from baseline on the Clinical Dementia Rating; secondary and exploratory endpoints included CSF tau biomarkers and tau PET imaging.
Biogen said the data give it confidence to advance diranersen into registrational development; the FDA granted the drug Fast Track designation for Alzheimer's in 2025.

stories.headline: Calif and Anthropic's Mythos Build First Public macOS Kernel Exploit on M5 Silicon, Bypassing MIE

key_facts.fact: Calif researchers, working with Anthropic's Mythos Preview, built a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit that bypasses Apple's Memory Integrity Enforcement (MIE) on M5 silicon — described as the first public exploit of its kind.
The chain is a data-only local privilege escalation against macOS 26.4.1 that starts as an unprivileged user using only normal system calls and ends with a root shell.
Calif says Apple spent roughly five years building MIE; its team built the exploit in five days, with bugs found on April 25 and a working exploit completed by May 1.
Apple confirmed it is reviewing the 55-page report Calif delivered in person at Apple Park; CEO Thai Duong said the attack 'couldn't have been pulled off by Mythos alone'.

stories.headline: Figure AI Humanoids Sort 28,000 Packages in 24-Hour Fully Autonomous Run

key_facts.fact: Figure AI on May 14 completed a 24-hour autonomous test of three humanoid robots — Bob, Frank and Gary — that ran without human control and sorted more than 28,000 packages.

The robots detect barcodes, place packages on conveyor belts using onboard cameras and AI reasoning, and run on Helix-02, a system combining vision, touch sensing, proprioception and whole-body control.
When a robot gets stuck or hits an unfamiliar situation, the Helix-02 system can trigger an autonomous reset and resume work with zero human intervention; the run was livestreamed online.
The benchmark builds on Figure's earlier work at BMW's Spartanburg, South Carolina plant, where Figure 02 robots have contributed to the movement of more than 90,000 parts.

stories.headline: Iceotope Raises $26M Series B for Precision Liquid Cooling as AI Racks Push Past 1MW

key_facts.fact: Sheffield-based Iceotope announced on May 14 a $26 million Series B funding round to advance its precision liquid cooling technology for AI and high-performance data centers.
The round was co-led by Two Seas Capital and Barclays Climate Ventures, with participation from existing investors Edinv, ABC Impact, Northern Gritstone and British Business Bank.
Iceotope said next-generation GPU and accelerator platforms are driving rack power densities toward 1 megawatt and beyond, rendering air cooling and direct-to-chip liquid cooling insufficient.

Iceotope's chassis-based approach replaces air with dielectric fluid circulated directly around server components inside a sealed chassis; flagship products include KUL BOX and KUL AI for high-density AI rack deployments.

stories.headline: Intel Begins Testing Production of Low-End Apple iPhone, iPad and Mac Chips on 18A-P

key_facts.fact: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reported on May 14 that Apple has kicked off low-end/legacy iPhone, iPad and Mac processor production at Intel on the 18A-P series using Foveros packaging.

Kuo said the order mix is roughly 80% iPhone, mirroring Apple's end-device sales mix, and that Apple views Intel as 'one of the very few, and arguably the most complete' foundry training alternatives to TSMC.
Apple believes TSMC's resources will continue tilting toward AI customers, motivating the dual-source strategy with Intel's Arizona fabs.
Intel's 18A-P is the company's first node to support Foveros Direct 3D hybrid bonding, using a pitch of less than 5 microns to stack multiple chiplets through TSVs.

stories.headline: Iran Lets ~30 Ships Including Chinese Vessels Cross Strait of Hormuz, Signals Waterway 'Open' to Cooperating Traffic

key_facts.fact: Iranian state media said about 30 vessels had crossed the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours on May 14, with semi-official Fars news agency reporting Iran had begun allowing transit for some Chinese vessels.

Iranian media reported more than 30 ships, including some linked to Chinese companies, transited the Strait overnight as Tehran signaled the waterway was 'open to all commercial ships' that cooperate with Iranian naval forces.

Trump said Xi offered China's help to open the Strait of Hormuz and pledged not to send military equipment to aid Iran in its war against the US and Israel; Xi also expressed interest in buying more US oil.

Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi urged BRICS+ at a New Delhi meeting on May 14 to condemn the US-Israel war on Iran as a violation of international law, calling Iran a 'victim of illegal expansionism and warmongering.'
Brent crude held flat at $105.63/bbl after retreating from an earlier intraday high of $107.13, while WTI was little changed at $101.03.

stories.headline: Kioxia Forecasts Record $8.2B Q1 Operating Profit, Announces Plans to List in the US

key_facts.fact: Kioxia on May 15 said it expects operating profit for the April–June quarter to reach ¥1.3 trillion ($8.2 billion), beating analyst estimates, as AI demand drives memory chip prices.

Kioxia reported full-year operating profit of ¥870.4 billion for the year ended March, up 92.7% year-over-year and beating estimates, and posted record quarterly earnings of ¥596.8 billion for the March quarter.

The company said it is preparing to list American depositary shares on a U.S. exchange to grow its investor base, following its Tokyo listing in late 2024 after being carved out of Toshiba by a Bain Capital-led consortium.
Kioxia is the world's best-performing major stock this year, with shares up roughly 300% year-to-date, riding a global NAND flash shortage driven by AI server demand.
Fiscal-year revenue rose 37% to ¥2.34 trillion, and profit attributable to owners of the parent reached ¥554.5 billion, more than doubling year-over-year, on AI-server and enterprise SSD demand.

stories.headline: Russia Pounds Kyiv With 670+ Drones and 56 Missiles, Killing at Least 24 in Largest Two-Day Aerial Assault of War

key_facts.fact: Russian overnight attack on May 14 killed at least 24 people, including two children, in Kyiv after 675 attack drones and 56 missiles were launched at Ukraine; air defenses downed 652 drones and 41 missiles.
Over Wednesday and Thursday combined, Russia launched 1,567 drones and at least 27 civilians were killed, the largest aerial barrage over a two-day window since the start of the invasion in 2022.

The attack came after a three-day US-brokered ceasefire expired late Monday and as Trump met Xi in Beijing; Ukrainian FM Andriy Sybiha said the strike showed Russia wanted to keep fighting despite Washington's peace push.
EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the bloc is finalizing a €6 billion ($7B) drone support package for Ukraine and would keep tightening sanctions on Russia's war economy.
Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu reiterated on May 14 that ending the war requires Ukraine to return to 'non-aligned, neutral and non-nuclear' status.

stories.headline: Microsoft Cancels Claude Code Licenses for Internal Devs, Mandates Shift to GitHub Copilot CLI by June 30

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is canceling thousands of internal Claude Code licenses by June 30, 2026, requiring its Experiences + Devices team to transition to GitHub Copilot CLI as the primary agentic command-line tool.
The move affects engineers working on Windows, Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams and Surface; the June 30 deadline aligns with the end of Microsoft's fiscal year, suggesting cost-cutting motivation.

Rajesh Jha, EVP of Microsoft's Experiences and Devices group, said in an internal memo that 'Copilot CLI has given us something especially important: a product we can help shape directly with GitHub for Microsoft's repos, workflows, security expectations, and engineering needs'.
Internal developers reportedly favored Claude Code over GitHub Copilot CLI since Microsoft opened access in December 2025; Anthropic models remain accessible to Microsoft engineers via Copilot CLI.

stories.headline: OPEC+ Plans Phased Quota Hikes Through September Even as Hormuz Blockage Drives Saudi Output to 36-Year Low

key_facts.fact: OPEC+ delegates said on May 14 the group aims to complete restoration of a 1.65 million bpd cut in three more monthly tranches through September, finishing on paper even though most members cannot actually deliver the barrels.

Saudi Arabia's output plunged to 6.3 million bpd in April, the lowest level since 1990, Kuwait is down to about a quarter of pre-war levels, and OPEC production has fallen ~9.7 million bpd (30%+) since the Iran war began Feb. 28.

The IEA said global oil supply has lost 12.8 million bpd since the war started, with cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers exceeding one billion barrels and inventories falling at a record pace.
OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast to 1.17 million bpd from 1.38 million bpd previously, while the IEA forecasts demand will contract by 420,000 bpd this year.

The next OPEC+ policy meeting is set for June 7 to decide July output levels; remaining members already approved a modest 188,000 bpd increase for June, with the UAE having formally exited OPEC on May 1.

stories.headline: OpenAI Brings Codex to ChatGPT Mobile App in Preview, Adds Remote SSH for Cloud Dev Environments

key_facts.fact: OpenAI rolled out a preview of Codex inside the ChatGPT mobile app on iOS and Android across all plans (including Free and Go) in supported regions on May 14.
From the phone, users can review outputs, approve commands, switch models or start new work, while files, credentials and project context stay on the connected machine where Codex runs.
Mobile support currently connects to the Codex app on macOS; Windows support is coming soon.
Alongside the mobile rollout, Remote SSH became generally available, letting Codex connect directly into managed remote dev environments via the desktop app's SSH config.

stories.headline: TSMC Forecasts $1.5T Chip Market by 2030, Says AI Wafer Demand to Rise 11x by 2026

key_facts.fact: TSMC told its 2026 Technology Symposium on May 14 that AI accelerator wafer demand is projected to grow 11-fold between 2022 and 2026, and raised its global semiconductor market forecast to exceed $1.5 trillion by 2030, up from a previous $1 trillion estimate.

Capacity for TSMC's 2nm and next-generation A16 nodes is projected to grow at a 70% CAGR from 2026 to 2028, while CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity is forecast to grow at more than 80% CAGR from 2022 to 2027.

TSMC plans to build nine phases of wafer fabs and advanced packaging facilities in 2026, and currently mass-produces a 5.5-reticle CoWoS at 98% yield, with plans for a 14-reticle, 20-HBM-stack version in 2028 and a 24-HBM-stack version in 2029.

TSMC said its Arizona output is expected to increase 1.8-fold year over year by 2026, with the first fab in production, tool move-in for fab 2 in 2H26, fab 3 under construction, and work on fab 4 and the site's first advanced-packaging facility set to begin this year.
AI and high-performance computing are expected to account for 55% of the $1.5 trillion market, followed by smartphones at 20% and automotive at 10%.

stories.headline: US Retail Sales Rise 0.5% and Jobless Claims Hit 211K as Iran-War Inflation Pressures Mount

key_facts.fact: US retail sales rose 0.5% in April after a downwardly revised 1.6% jump in March, the Commerce Department said on May 14; gasoline prices rose 12.3% in April amid the Iran war.
Initial jobless claims rose 12,000 to a seasonally adjusted 211,000 for the week ended May 9, above the 205,000 forecast; continuing claims climbed 24,000 to 1.782 million.

US import prices jumped 1.9% in April, much more than expected; producer prices recorded their biggest monthly gain in over four years and consumer prices rose 3.8% YoY, the largest annual jump in three years.

Markets price little chance of any Fed rate cuts this year, with odds of a hike climbing to about 39% after the PPI report; the Fed has held its benchmark rate at 3.5%-3.75% as Iran-war inflation proves sticky.
Excluding gas, retail sales rose only 0.3% in April, with furniture and clothing stores slipping as higher gas costs eat into discretionary spending.

stories.headline: Korea's WIRobotics Raises $68M Series B to Accelerate Humanoid Commercialization

key_facts.fact: WIRobotics on May 14 announced a KRW 95 billion (~$68 million) Series B funding round to accelerate humanoid commercialization and expand into integrated robotics platforms.
The round was led by J. Investment, with participation from InterVest, Hana Ventures, Smilegate Investment, SBVA, NH Investment & Securities, Company K Partners, GU Investment and FuturePlay.

Cumulative sales of WIRobotics' ALLEX humanoid platform have surpassed 3,000 units across Europe, China, Türkiye and Japan, and the company plans to launch a research-focused humanoid platform later this year.
The company has been selected for the second cohort of the Physical AI Fellowship powered by AWS, Nvidia and MassRobotics.

stories.headline: xAI Launches Grok Build, an Agentic Coding CLI, in Beta for SuperGrok Heavy Subscribers

key_facts.fact: xAI launched on May 14 an early beta of Grok Build, a coding agent and CLI for professional software engineering, available first to SuperGrok Heavy subscribers.
Grok Build supports a 'plan, review, approve' flow, MCP servers, AGENTS.md and parallel subagents that can run in their own git worktrees.
SuperGrok Heavy is xAI's top consumer subscription, priced at roughly $300 per month and aimed at professional developers and researchers.
The release positions xAI to rival Anthropic's Claude Code in agentic terminal coding tools.
